title: improve-tool-calling-execution-ergonomics-multi-tool-parallel-retries
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Enhances tool-calling ergonomics: multi-tool orchestration, parallel tool execution, deterministic tool-result injection, and robust retry semantics. Backwards compatible with existing OpenAI-compatible tool payloads. See docs for new API flags and examples.
description: Motivation: Customers increasingly build chains that call multiple external tools in a single turn (search, calendar, code-exec, db). We observed two common pain points: 1) surface ergonomics for specifying multi-tool/parallel calls and deterministic result injection into model context and 2) brittle execution when transient tool failures require coordinated retries while preserving model-visible telemetry. This PR implements a cross-cutting set of API surface and runtime changes to address multi-tool orchestration, parallel execution, tool-result injection, and retry semantics while preserving OpenAI compatibility. Changes: - Introduces a new optional 'tools_execution' object in the OpenAI-compat layer that accepts an ordered list of tool calls with execution hints (parallel/group/serial) and explicit injection tokens. Default behavior remains unchanged if not provided. - Runtime: adds a lightweight orchestrator that schedules tool workers across the serving pool, enabling parallel calls when hints permit and aggregating results deterministically. - Result injection: deterministic placeholder tokens are emitted into the streaming transcript so the model sees stable markers for tool outputs; the runtime supports both in-band injection (stream) and out-of-band metadata for clients who prefer separate channels. - Retries: idempotent retry metadata (request_id + idempotency_key) and a retry policy framework (per-tool backoff, max attempts, fail-mode: continue-with-empty / abort / fallback-tool). Retries are coordinated so the model receives only final injected results (no noisy partial failures). - Observability: new tracing spans, per-tool latency histograms, and retry counters exposed to Console and tracing backends. - OpenAI compatibility updates: openai-compat adapter now maps existing function-calling fields to the new execution hints, and preserves legacy behavior when clients submit simple single-tool 'function_call' requests. - Streaming stability: improved handshake for stream clients so tool-run events (start/complete/result) are streamed as structured events; streaming reconnects replay the last stable injection token to avoid model ambiguity. Compatibility and migration: default remains backward compatible. New flags are opt-in: tools_execution and execution_policy. Existing function_call usage continues to work unchanged. We add clear migration docs and examples. Testing and QA: unit tests for orchestrator logic, integration tests with redwood-examples/tooling harness simulating parallel tools, load tests in perf-canary to validate throughput, and new e2e flaky-retry scenarios captured in incident-bot harness. Rollout: feature gated behind FF_TOOL_ORCHESTRATION; staged rollout to internal tenants, then canary customers, then general availability. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (ENG-1024) linked - [x] Runtime implementation - [x] OpenAI-compat mapping - [x] Streaming event format and docs - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Perf validation (perf-canary) - [x] Docs and examples (redwood-docs, redwood-examples) - [x] Feature-flag + rollout plan
commits: feat(orchestrator): add multi-tool execution scheduler and worker pool
feat(api): add tools_execution hints to openai-compat payload mapping
fix(stream): stable injection tokens and reconnect replay
chore(tests): add integration tests for parallel tool execution
docs(api): document tools_execution and retry policies
review_comments: Evan Liu: Nice work — oriented comments inline around backpressure behavior. Please ensure we have a clear fallback for failing sync tools.
Priya Shah (author): responded — added coordinated fail-mode with explicit options and updated docs to show examples.
Miguel Fernandez: Concern about idempotency_key surface. Suggest using explicit per-tool keys and auto-generating when omitted. Marked as resolved after change.
Aisha Patel: Noted perf regression on small batches — we optimized worker backpressure and added perf-canary tests; approving once metrics are green.
merge_commit_message:
Improve tool-calling execution ergonomics: multi-tool orchestration, parallel execution, stable result injection, coordinated retries

See ENG-1024 and ENG-1099 for design and test matrices.
notes_on_deployment: Feature gated by FF_TOOL_ORCHESTRATION. Start with internal flag -> canary accounts -> GA. Monitor tool.retry_count, tool.latency_p95, streaming.injection_replays. Revert path: disable flag and drain running tool orchestrations.
notes_on_backward_compatibility: If tools_execution is not provided, behavior is identical to existing function_call semantics. OpenAI-compat adapter will auto-map single function_call into tools_execution[0]. Clients opting into parallel/group semantics must handle new structured streaming events documented in streaming/protocol.md.
security_considerations: Tool calls can surface external data. We added per-tool policy labels and validators in api/handlers/tool_calls.py and KMS integration checks for sensitive outputs. Tools running in Private deployments honor VPC egress rules. Security-scan flagged a transient dependency; upgraded vendor package to mitigate.
